turns.content: First: the final fleet's cutover finished overnight but the board still shows it in progress because the automation only polls weekly. Force the refresh so closeout starts from a green board instead of a stale one. While you are in the board automation, drop the weekly poll to daily for the archive period; a closeout board that lags reality by a week generates exactly the kind of stale-status questions we are trying to retire.
Forced the board refresh; all fleets show migrated and the stalled-fleet annotations are archived with the blocker thread linked.

Purge the registry's dead entries from the decommissioned collectors; a third of the list is tombstones at this point and it makes the freshness panel scroll for days during reviews. Keep a dated export of the purged list in the drills folder though, because the decommission audit in the fall will want to reconcile tombstones against the asset registry.
Purged the tombstones and added an auto-expiry for future decommissions; the freshness panel fits on one screen again.

The old registration path can be turned off now. Disable it behind the flag first, full removal next release, so a straggler gets a clear error instead of silence when they try it. The error should name the flag and link the guide section directly; stragglers hitting it will be mid-provisioning and in no mood to search.
Disabled the old path behind the flag with a clear error pointing at the new handshake; removal is ticketed for next release.

Docs final pass: the collectors guide accumulated three migration-era callouts that are now just permanent behaviour. Fold them into the main text and drop the temporary framing before closeout. Have someone who did not write the guide read the folded version cold, since steady-state text written by migration folks tends to assume context newcomers will not have.
Folded the callouts into the main sections and removed the migration framing; the guide reads as steady-state now.

The migration board itself should be archived once we call the heartbeat decision, with a summary page up top. Prep that so archiving is one click later today. The summary page should lead with the two numbers people actually ask about: total fleets moved and days from first cutover to last.
Prepped the board archive with a summary page of dates, fleets, and open follow-ups; one click when you call it.

Retro: book the migration retro for Thursday and pull the blocker thread and the gap analysis into the outline beforehand so we are not assembling context live. Book the room with the good screen as well; the gap-analysis charts are unreadable on the small one and half the retro is going to be chart reading.
Booked Thursday's retro and seeded the outline with the blocker thread, the gap analysis, and the closeout summary.

Rerun came back clean, so closing it out: stretch the collector heartbeat to 75 seconds fleet-wide from tonight's config push, restart annotations stay on, and the registry expiry stays defined in missed beats so nothing else needs retuning. Archive the board once the push lands.
Config push scheduled for tonight with the stretch included, annotations left on, and the board archives automatically once the push confirms.

8| // heartbeater sends the periodic collector beat carrying the health
9| // summary: queue depth, last-batch age, and the config revision the
10| // collector is running. The interval comes from deployment config;
11| // the pre-reorg fleet's 60 seconds default lives only in history.
12| type heartbeater struct {
13| 	every  time.Duration
14| 	missed int
15| 	send   func(context.Context, beat) error
16| }
17| 
18| type beat struct {
19| 	queueDepth int
20| 	lastBatch  time.Time
21| 	configRev  string
22| }
23| 
24| // run sends beats on the configured interval until cancelled. A send
25| // failure is counted and skipped, never retried inline: the next beat
26| // is a fresher summary than a delayed copy of the last one, and the
27| // registry treats missed beats as the health signal anyway.
28| func (h *heartbeater) run(ctx context.Context) {
29| 	t := time.NewTicker(h.every)
30| 	defer t.Stop()
31| 	for {
32| 		select {
33| 		case <-ctx.Done():
34| 			return
35| 		case <-t.C:
36| 			if err := h.send(ctx, h.snapshot()); err != nil {
37| 				h.missed++
38| 			}
39| 		}
40| 	}
41| }
